title: Rigveda 9.93: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.93: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.93 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 721r-721v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.text: <sup>1</sup>TEN sisters, pouring out the rain together, swift-moving thinkers of the sage, adorn him. Hither hath run the gold-hued Child of Sûrya and reached the vat like a fleet vigorous courser.

translation.original_ref: RV 9.93.2-5 (aṣṭaka 7, adhyāya 4, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 721v
translation.original_text:
2sam mā̱tṛbhi̱r na śiśu̍r vāvaśā̱no vṛṣā̍ dadhanve puru̱vāro̍ a̱dbhiḥ | maryo̱ na yoṣā̍m a̱bhi ni̍ṣkṛ̱taṁ yan saṁ ga̍cchate ka̱laśa̍ u̱sriyā̍bhiḥ ||
3u̱ta pra pi̍pya̱ ūdha̱r aghnyā̍yā̱ indu̱r dhārā̍bhiḥ sacate sume̱dhāḥ | mū̱rdhāna̱ṁ gāva̱ḥ paya̍sā ca̱mūṣv a̱bhi śrī̍ṇanti̱ vasu̍bhi̱r na ni̱ktaiḥ ||
4sa no̍ de̱vebhi̍ḥ pavamāna ra̱dendo̍ ra̱yim a̱śvina̍ṁ vāvaśā̱naḥ | ra̱thi̱rā̱yatā̍m uśa̱tī pura̍ṁdhir asma̱drya1̱̍g ā dā̱vane̱ vasū̍nām ||
5nū no̍ ra̱yim upa̍ māsva nṛ̱vanta̍m punā̱no vā̱tāpya̍ṁ vi̱śvaśca̍ndram | pra va̍ndi̱tur i̍ndo tā̱ry āyu̍ḥ prā̱tar ma̱kṣū dhi̱yāva̍sur jagamyāt ||
translation.text:
2Even as a youngling crying to his mothers, the bounteous Steer hath flowed along to waters. As youth to damsel, so with milk he hastens on to the. chose meeting-place, the beaker.
3Yea, swollen is the udder of the milch-cow: thither in streams goes very sapient Indu. The kine make ready, as with new-washed treasures, the Head and Chief with milk within the vessels.
4With all the Gods, O Indu Pavamâna, while thou art roaring send us wealth in horses. Hither upon her car come willing Plenty, inclined to us, to give us of her treasures.
5Now unto us mete riches, while they cleansethee, all-glorious, swelling wealth, with store of heroes. Long be his life who worships, thee, O Indu. May he, enriched with prayer, come soon and early.

Verses 9.93.2-5 end on this page; 9.93.2 begins on fol. 721r (numbered 38r by the scribe).
